A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original behavior-cloning simulations, neural-collapse measurements, pretraining comparisons in Table 1, and robotic pushing experiments in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: V3 retains these original results and adds experiments on Lunar Lander, block stacking, encoder initialization, DINOv2 pretraining, and visually complex pushing environments.

M1.justification: V3 adds a discrete image-control instantiation using ResNet18, an MLP projection and action decoder, and cross-entropy supervision over four actions (Section 2, Appendix A). The continuous-control REPO classification and NC-pretraining procedure remain unchanged. Appendix F's explicit loss weights document the existing procedure rather than establish a revised loss.

E1.justification: V1 studies a state-based double integrator and simulated and real planar pushing. V3 adds image-based Lunar Lander and MimicGen block stacking, substantially broadening task coverage. It also introduces simulated pushing with a LineMod background and real pushing with distracting objects and paintings, extending visual-environment coverage.

E2.justification: V3 adds frozen versus finetuned and ImageNet-pretrained versus randomly initialized ResNet comparisons in Table 2. Table 3 introduces a DINOv2 baseline within the NC-pretraining comparison, although DINOv2 already appeared in v1's architecture experiments. These extend comparisons within existing model families; the original comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: New protocols include Lunar Lander behavior cloning from 500 PPO demonstrations using four input frames and 600 training epochs, and block stacking with 1,000 demonstrations and 107,590 samples. The added complex-background robot experiment uses 200 demonstrations and 10 test tasks. Table 2 introduces initialization and freezing controls. These are added experimental designs; Appendix F's schedules for existing Table 1 experiments are newly disclosed details.

E4.justification: V3 adds analyses isolating ImageNet initialization and encoder finetuning, tests clustering and pretraining under complex visual backgrounds, and checks NC pretraining with DINOv2 (Appendices D, G.1, G.6 and Section 5). V1's k-means, REPO-granularity, LSTM, low-data, and continual-finetuning analyses remain present, often relocated.

E5.justification: The shared diffusion-model experiments retain means and standard-deviation bands over three random seeds, while LSTM results remain single-seed. V3 introduces no new confidence intervals, significance tests, or explicit repetition scheme. Additional tables and curves do not establish a change in uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the original clean-background robot success counts are unchanged. V3 adds clustering curves for Lunar Lander, stacking, and complex-background pushing; initialization results in Table 2; and DINOv2 pretraining results in Table 3, including 0.3747 versus 0.4602 on O. The new complex-background robot experiment reports 9/10 successes with NC pretraining versus 6/10 for baseline using 200 demonstrations. These are additional conditions, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The double-integrator policy, neural-collapse definitions, CDNV and norm/angular metrics, and REPO construction retain their mathematical substance. Equations are relocated and renumbered. Neither version provides a formal proof of control-oriented clustering, and v3 adds no theorem or substantive derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion broaden the principal clustering claim from planar pushing to both discrete and continuous image-based control. V3 explicitly claims clustering by natural action labels in Lunar Lander and by control-oriented classes in pushing and stacking. The existing claim of improved low-data performance through NC pretraining is retained.

C2.justification: Appendix D substantially expands the interpretation of pretrained representations: ImageNet initialization benefits finetuning in visually complex scenes but shows little benefit on clean pushing, while frozen features remain inadequate. V3 also explicitly identifies ground-truth pose requirements as a scaling limitation for multiple or deformable objects and clarifies that extra pose information is unnecessary at test time.

D1.justification: Appendix F newly specifies the NC loss as 0.1 × CDNV + 10 × (STDNorm + STDAngle), four shuffled batches per pretraining epoch, and 50 pretraining plus 50 joint-training epochs versus 100 baseline epochs. These clarify previously underspecified experiments. Appendix A adds Lunar Lander architecture and expert-generation details, and the stacking section identifies the core stack_d0 dataset.

R1.justification: V3 adds references supporting Gym, MimicGen, LineMod, PPO, RL Baselines3 Zoo, and MuJoCo, and removes the Huh et al. representation-hypothesis citation. The related-work discussion is otherwise retained from v1 Appendix D as v3 Appendix I, with no substantial change in positioning against neural-collapse or imitation-learning research.

P1.justification: V3 rewrites the abstract around discrete and continuous control, expands the introductory motivation, and reorganizes the central exposition into separate discrete- and continuous-control sections. Action-based classification and continual-finetuning discussion move into dedicated appendices, while the conclusion gains an explicit limitations paragraph. This substantially changes the narrative structure.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is extensively redesigned to show three tasks, and the classification diagrams are revised and expanded. V1 Figure 5 is split between v3 Figures 6 and 21, while continual-learning figures move to the appendix. V3 adds new task plots, Tables 2 and 3, and complex-background robot montages; Figure 10 now juxtaposes clean and complex scenes.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially strengthens v1's narrow empirical foundation through additional control tasks, visually complex environments, and initialization/freezing controls. Appendix F resolves important omissions in documenting the central pretraining procedure, while the explicit pose-annotation limitation improves scope calibration. Together these improve evidential support, interpretation, and reproducibility. Pretraining benefits remain demonstrated principally on pushing, and robot evaluations remain small, but these limits do not outweigh the gains.
